sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible to apply while completing a mathematics bachelor's or equivalent; central minimum GPA 3.0.
Successful preparation usually includes two semesters of abstract algebra (or one plus applied algebra),
proof-based analysis including complex analysis, and several further proof courses. Fall PhD admission only; no
standalone master's. [s1] [s2] [s5]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare online application, transcripts, CV, statement and three referees. Upload proof of at least two
academic years of English-medium study and email gradapp@nd.edu to confirm the language exemption.
Request a fee waiver with evidence if needed before paying. [s2] [s3] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior supervisor agreement was listed as a prerequisite. Use current faculty research pages to identify
matches; 2027 availability remains unconfirmed. Jorza and Lim hold practice appointments, and Székelyhidi is
adjunct from Northwestern; do not treat them as ordinary available Notre Dame PhD supervisors. [s1] [s11] [s12]
Portal workflow [Conflict]
Slate application: upload materials rather than send them directly; invitations go immediately on adding
referees; status page tracks receipt. FAQ and general page disagree about modifying submitted materials -
confirm specific replacements with gradapp@nd.edu. [s3] [s5]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Program listing updated September 28, 2026, but January 7 deadline lacks an explicit entry year. Funding is
explicitly 2026-27, not the 2027-28 incoming package. [s4] [s8]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
If not exempt: TOEFL 80 with speaking 23 on the old scale; current FAQ gives 4.5 overall and 4.0 each section
on the new scale; IELTS 7.0 or Duolingo 120. Scores valid two years. Math can review lower speaking scores
using additional evidence/interview. Current Math/FAQ accept Duolingo although an older requirements page
omits it. [s2] [s3] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
At least two academic years of study at an English-medium institution qualifies; a completed or expected
UChicago undergraduate education should meet the Math rule. Upload transcript or medium-of-instruction
certification in Test Scores instead of scores, then email gradapp@nd.edu for confirmation. [s2] [s3]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional; unofficial results can be reviewed, valid five years. No minimum. Optional is not a promise that
submitted scores are ignored. [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional; strong scores may help, especially when the committee knows less about the applicant's
undergraduate institution. No minimum. Math reports limited weight historically. [s2]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three required; central system permits up to five. [s2] [s3]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Select fellowships use automatic consideration and admitting-department nominations. No separate initial
applicant reference requirement was published; individual fellowship follow-up may differ. [s9]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Adding a recommender immediately sends the electronic invitation, before submission. Interfolio can be used
through Slate's electronic process; paper letters are not accepted. [s3]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Letters can arrive before submission; application can be submitted with letters outstanding after the
recommenders have been entered/invited. Referee details can be edited afterward. [s3]

Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Application status page records receipt; allow about one business day for processing and up to 24 hours for the
initial status email. [s3]
Updating and reusing letters [Conflict]
Referees can be edited after submission. A new-cycle application requires resubmitting materials and an
updated statement; scores already held may be reused if valid. Replacement of an already uploaded letter is
not publicly resolved. Central FAQ permits postsubmission amendments while the general requirements page
says submitted applications cannot be changed. [s3] [s5]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
University science doctoral standard for 2026-27: USD 40,590 for twelve months; select fellows up to USD
50,000. This is a current university benchmark, not a confirmed Fall 2027 Math award. Math admits receive
living support and tuition. Tuition scholarships cover fees except a small activity fee; eligible fully funded
students' standard 2026-27 health premium subsidy covers the premium. [s1] [s8]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Math guarantees five years subject to good standing; sixth year may be granted at committee discretion. First
year is fellowship support without teaching, later years normally assistantship. [s1] [s10]

International eligibility [Standing rule]
Math support is offered to admitted students, including international applicants; select fellowships state all
admitted full-time students are considered, while individual award eligibility differs. [s1] [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Maintain academic and teaching standing; renewal reviewed in spring. Outside mathematics-related work
requires permission; more than two hours weekly needs advisor and graduate-director approval, including
summer. Other externally funded duties require prior approval. [s10]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Select fellowships: automatic applicant consideration, competitive departmental nomination. Summer research
requires the appropriate registration and local procedures after enrollment; not a separate initial admissions
essay. [s9] [s10]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Select fellowships include Notebaert, Schmitt, Voll, Naughton and Deans' awards; eligibility is award-specific.
Grants and Fellowships office supports external applications. Standard science figure and maximum fellowship
amount should not be added together. [s8] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75 per application, preferably credit card; check payable to University of Notre Dame can be sent to
Graduate Recruitment and Admissions, 115 Main Building, Notre Dame IN 46556. [s7]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Domestic and international financial-need requests are eligible. Upload supporting evidence (for example
bank/mobile-money statement, pay stub or institutional aid letter); processing typically 48 hours. Some
automatic categories appear after first two sections. Application may be submitted before waiver approval.
Math has limited case-by-case waivers: email Mark Behrens, mbehren1@nd.edu, with reasons. No separate
date published. [s2] [s7]

Optional; unofficial results can be reviewed, valid five years. No minimum. Optional is not a promise that
submitted scores are ignored. [s2]

undergraduate institution. No minimum. Math reports limited weight historically. [s2]

translation plus original. Do not send paper/direct electronic records for review; official final documents
required after acceptance before enrollment. [s3] [s5]

Strongly recommended list of all mathematics beyond calculus, including textbooks; particularly helpful for

obscure the content. [s2]

applicant reference requirement was published; individual fellowship follow-up may differ. [s9]

recommenders have been entered/invited. Referee details can be edited afterward. [s3]

application. [s2] [s6]

Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
University science doctoral standard for 2026-27: USD 40,590 for twelve months; select fellows up to USD
50,000. This is a current university benchmark, not a confirmed Fall 2027 Math award. Math admits receive
living support and tuition. Tuition scholarships cover fees except a small activity fee; eligible fully funded
students' standard 2026-27 health premium subsidy covers the premium. [s1] [s8]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Math guarantees five years subject to good standing; sixth year may be granted at committee discretion. First
year is fellowship support without teaching, later years normally assistantship. [s1] [s10]

Math support is offered to admitted students, including international applicants; select fellowships state all

Maintain academic and teaching standing; renewal reviewed in spring. Outside mathematics-related work

Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
University science doctoral standard for 2026-27: USD 40,590 for twelve months; select fellows up to USD
50,000. This is a current university benchmark, not a confirmed Fall 2027 Math award. Math admits receive
living support and tuition. Tuition scholarships cover fees except a small activity fee; eligible fully funded
students' standard 2026-27 health premium subsidy covers the premium. [s1] [s8]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Math guarantees five years subject to good standing; sixth year may be granted at committee discretion. First
year is fellowship support without teaching, later years normally assistantship. [s1] [s10]

Math support is offered to admitted students, including international applicants; select fellowships state all
admitted full-time students are considered, while individual award eligibility differs. [s1] [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Maintain academic and teaching standing; renewal reviewed in spring. Outside mathematics-related work
requires permission; more than two hours weekly needs advisor and graduate-director approval, including
summer. Other externally funded duties require prior approval. [s10]

requires the appropriate registration and local procedures after enrollment; not a separate initial admissions
essay. [s9] [s10]

Select fellowships include Notebaert, Schmitt, Voll, Naughton and Deans' awards; eligibility is award-specific.

amount should not be added together. [s8] [s9]

USD 75 per application, preferably credit card; check payable to University of Notre Dame can be sent to
Graduate Recruitment and Admissions, 115 Main Building, Notre Dame IN 46556. [s7]

Domestic and international financial-need requests are eligible. Upload supporting evidence (for example
bank/mobile-money statement, pay stub or institutional aid letter); processing typically 48 hours. Some
